pool.text: The oldest written evidence for the name Osaka dates back to this year.
Toyotomi Hideyoshi constructed Osaka Castle in place of the destroyed temple.
The Rice Exchange was established in Dojima to sell unharvested rice.
Writer Hamamatsu Utakuni published his book Setsuyo Ochiboshu explaining kanji changes.
The kanji character 阪 became the official name after the Meiji Restoration.
The modern municipality was established by government ordinance with a small initial area.
Nomura Securities, the first brokerage firm in Japan, was founded here.
The Ad Council Japan was founded and is based in the city.
The Symphony Hall was built as the first classical music concert hall.
Numerous international events have been held including the APEC Summit.
The Osaka Museum of History opened in a 13-story modern building.
Umeda Arts Theater opened after relocating from its former theater.
The Hanjotei opened, which is entirely dedicated to traditional rakugo performances.
The 300-meter tall Abeno Harukas opened and became the country's tallest building.
The city officially ended its sister city relationship with San Francisco.
A second referendum to merge wards into semi-autonomous wards was voted down.
